messages.author: f05273cf5f528e54
messages.subject: DDM and delta parameter
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have two questions about the choiceRT_ddm model:
1. Is there a reason that the delta parameter is not reparametrized (except for the non-centered reparametrization)? From my understanding, delta > 0, so I wonder why in your stan models (choiceRT_ddm) this paramater is not constrained?
2. In my task I have different levels of visual coherence (0.05, 0.1, 0.35, 0.5). Should it affect the delta parameter somehow or should I fit the wiener distribution with one fixed delta nevertheless?

Thank you! (And thanks for this great package.)

Daniel

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: DDM and delta parameter
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for using it! 

re (1), I think we originally had it so that delta>0, but then another user requested a change since there are certain task designs wherein a delta<0 may make sense. 

re (2), this would depend on the theory you are aiming to test, I assume. Unfortunately, the current structure does not allow for estimating different deltas within conditions for the DDM, although the LBA model is currently equipped to do so. That said, I would check out the LBA model if you are interested in condition effects, or alternatively something like HDDM (http://ski.clps.brown.edu/hddm_docs/) if you would like to stick with the DDM. 

Best,
Nate

Thanks, Nate.

re (1) - thanks! Just wanted to make sure I didn't miss anything.
re (2) - the issue here is that my data recovery is pretty bad even if I use RWiener package to generate random draws with one coherence level. wiener_rng is not yet implemented in Stan so I wonder how the data recovery worked for you and how well was it when you created this package?

Thanks!

Daniel
